Lecture 2c: Tapered Streams 101

Week 2 · GEOG 4/594 · Junjie Chen, PhD, PH · junchen@pdx.edu

A step-by-step ArcGIS Pro demo: vary the width of rivers and streams by flow for a more realistic map.

Contents
  1. Tapered Streams 101
  2. Overview
  3. Get your data - NHDPlus
  4. Download NHDPlus HR from the National Map

  10. For More Information

Slide 1 Tapered Streams 101

  • How to vary the size of rivers and streams for added realism

Slide 2 Overview

  • Symbolize rivers and streams by an attribute that relates to size for a more realistic look to your map.

Slide 3 Get your data - NHDPlus

  • NHDPlus High Resolution – the National Hydrography Dataset Plus (USGS)
  • Pick the data to download in the USGS National Map Downloader

Slide 4 Download NHDPlus HR from the National Map

Slide 5 Import and Join

  • Import the Flowlines (NHDFlowline in this case) and the table with the size attribute (NHDPlusEROMMA) you want to use to inform the symbology.
  • This demo will use FlowEstARunoffMA as the size attribute.
  • Then Join the mean annual flow data to the Flowlines layer using the NHDPlusID as the join field.

Slide 6 Use Statistics to evaluate stream size

  • Open the attribute table for the NHDFlowline layer and right click on the new field. Click on Statistics in the dropdown menu to get info about your dataset.
  • Use this information to inform your definition query (the next step).

Slide 7 Reduce the number of features

  • Use a definition query to reduce the number of features shown on the map.
  • Right click on the NHDFlowline layer and click Properties, then choose Definition Query.
  • First map: every flowline is drawn — too much stuff! Last map: after the query, only streams > 55 ft³/s (cfs).

Slide 8 Symbolize the Features

  • Right click on the NHDFlowline layer and choose symbology.
  • Choose Graduated Symbols from the dropdown menu
  • Adjust the Method, Classes, and Min and Max size to change the look of your tapered rivers and streams.

Slide 9 Ta-da! Tapered Streams

  • The Willamette River and its larger tributaries are now shown with streams that taper by mean annual flow in six classes from 0.6 pt to 3 pt.
  • More classes = smoother looking tapering

Slide 10 For More Information

  • Esri: Stream tapering adds realism to your map (the technique used in this presentation)
  • Esri: Symbolizing rivers and streams with proportional symbols (a similar technique)
  • Anita Graser: Better river styles with tapered lines (for QGIS users)
